CSCE 101.description: History, application, and social impact of computers; problem-solving, algorithm development, AI, applications software, and programming in a procedural language.
CSCE 101.subject: CSCE
CSCE 101.title: Introduction to Computer and Programming Concepts using AI Tools

CSCE 102.description: Introduction to web design and development. Covers HTML, CSS, JavaScript, AI tools, web design best practices, layout, content management, accessibility, usability, and search engine optimization.
CSCE 102.subject: CSCE
CSCE 102.title: Web Design and Development using AI Tools

CSCE 104.description: Fundamental algorithms and processes used in business information systems. Development and representation of programming logic. Introduction to implementation using a high-level programming language.
CSCE 104.subject: CSCE
CSCE 104.title: Program Design and Development

CSCE 106.description: Introduction to computer applications in science and engineering. Programming exercises in a high-level language.
CSCE 106.subject: CSCE
CSCE 106.title: Scientific Applications Programming

CSCE 145.description: Problem-solving, algorithmic design, and programming. Three lectures and two laboratory hours per week.
CSCE 145.subject: CSCE
CSCE 145.title: Algorithmic Design I

CSCE 146.description: Rigorous development of algorithms and computer programs; elementary data structures.
CSCE 146.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 145 or CSCE 106; C or better in MATH 111 or higher (or by Math Placement Test score into MATH 115 or higher math).
CSCE 146.subject: CSCE
CSCE 146.title: Algorithmic Design II

CSCE 180.description: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence and its applications. Overview of AI topics and applications, including machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, knowledge representation, statistical inference, and symbolic manipulation.
CSCE 180.subject: CSCE
CSCE 180.title: Artificial Intelligence for All

CSCE 190.description: An introduction to the field of computing: trends in computing technology, the profession, and careers; subdisciplines in computing; the nature of research and development.
CSCE 190.subject: CSCE
CSCE 190.title: Computing in the Modern World

CSCE 201.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of computer security, including security policies, authentification, digital certificates, firewalls, malicious code, legal and ethical issues, and incident handling.
CSCE 201.subject: CSCE
CSCE 201.title: Introduction to Computer Security

CSCE 205.description: Introduction to computer applications in business. Programming exercises in COBOL.
CSCE 205.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: MGSC 290 or CSCE 101 or above.
CSCE 205.subject: CSCE
CSCE 205.title: Business Applications Programming

CSCE 207.description: The Unix programming environment: I/O programming, Unix processes, fork, exec, pipes and signals, and tools.
CSCE 207.subject: CSCE
CSCE 207.title: UNIX System Administration

CSCE 209.description: Programming and application development using selected programming languages. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title.
CSCE 209.subject: CSCE
CSCE 209.title: Special Topics in Computer Programming

CSCE 210.description: Number representation, data formats, CPU and memory organization, assembly language, I/O and peripherals, computer networks. Students may not apply both CSCE 210 and CSCE 212 to any minor or major program of study.
CSCE 210.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in CSCE 145, CSCE 104, CSCE 205, CSCE 106, or CSCE 207.
CSCE 210.subject: CSCE
CSCE 210.title: Computer Hardware Foundations

CSCE 211.description: Number systems, Boolean algebra, logic design, sequential machines.
CSCE 211.subject: CSCE
CSCE 211.title: Digital Logic Design

CSCE 212.description: Computer architecture, components. and organization; memory addressing; Input/Output; instruction sets; interrupts; assembly-language programming. Students may not apply both CSCE 210 and CSCE 212 to any minor or major program of study.
CSCE 212.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in CSCE 211 and D or better in either CSCE 145 or CSCE 106.
CSCE 212.subject: CSCE
CSCE 212.title: Introduction to Computer Architecture

CSCE 215.description: UNIX operating system, user-level system commands, and programming tools. UNIX scripting languages.
CSCE 215.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 145 or CSCE 106 .
CSCE 215.subject: CSCE
CSCE 215.title: UNIX/Linux Fundamentals

CSCE 240.description: Pointers; memory management; advanced programming language structures: operator overloading, iterators, multiple inheritance, polymorphism, templates, virtual functions; Unix programming environment.
CSCE 240.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: CSCE 215, C or better in CSCE 146.
CSCE 240.subject: CSCE
CSCE 240.title: Advanced Programming Techniques

CSCE 242.description: Web technologies to support client-server computing. Implementation of client-server applications.
CSCE 242.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 146.
CSCE 242.subject: CSCE
CSCE 242.title: Web Applications

CSCE 245.description: Advanced object-oriented concepts and techniques; multiple inheritance; memory management; operator overloading; polymorphism; performance issues.
CSCE 245.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 146.
CSCE 245.subject: CSCE
CSCE 245.title: Object-Oriented Programming Techniques

CSCE 247.description: Fundamentals of software design and development; software implementation strategies; object-oriented design techniques; functional design techniques; design patterns; design process; source control; testing.
CSCE 247.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 146.
CSCE 247.subject: CSCE
CSCE 247.title: Software Engineering

CSCE 274.description: Design and control of robots. Interactions between robots, sensing, actuation, and computation.
CSCE 274.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 240.
CSCE 274.subject: CSCE
CSCE 274.title: Robotic Applications and Design

CSCE 304.description: Systematic problem definition, solution formulation, and computer implementation for business and related areas. Internet and database applications. Programming exercises in a high-level programming language.
CSCE 304.subject: CSCE
CSCE 304.title: Applied Problem Solving and Programming

CSCE 311.description: Operating system structure and function; process implementation, scheduling, and synchronization; memory management; security; naming protection; resource allocation; network file systems.
CSCE 311.subject: CSCE
CSCE 311.title: Operating Systems

CSCE 313.description: Fundamentals of embedded systems: hardware components, software components, hardware/software interface design, and hardware/software co-design.
CSCE 313.subject: CSCE
CSCE 313.title: Embedded Systems

CSCE 317.description: System-level modeling and evaluation of computer systems: requirements elicitation and specification, architectural design, reliability and performance evaluation, Markov modeling, life-cycle cost analysis, project management.
CSCE 317.subject: CSCE
CSCE 317.title: Computer Systems Engineering

CSCE 330.description: Formal specification of syntax and semantics; structure of algorithms; list processing and string manipulation languages; statement types, control structures, and interfacing procedures.
CSCE 330.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: CSCE 240; MATH 174 or MATH 374 or MATH 574.
CSCE 330.subject: CSCE
CSCE 330.title: Programming Language Structures

CSCE 350.description: Techniques for representing and processing information, including the use of lists, trees, and graphs; analysis of algorithms; sorting, searching, and hashing techniques.
CSCE 350.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in CSCE 240; D or better in MATH 174, MATH 374, or MATH 574; D or better in MATH 141 or MATH 122.
CSCE 350.subject: CSCE
CSCE 350.title: Data Structures and Algorithms

CSCE 355.description: Basic theoretical principles of computing as modeled by formal languages, grammars, automata, and Turing machines; fundamental limits of computation.
CSCE 355.subject: CSCE
CSCE 355.title: Foundations of Computation

CSCE 390.description: Professional issues in the information technology professions; history and social context of computing; professional responsibilities; privacy; intellectual property; risks and liabilities of computer-based systems.
CSCE 390.subject: CSCE
CSCE 390.title: Professional Issues in Computer Science and Engineering

CSCE 415.description: Introduction to the large scale computer systems used by businesses to support thousands of simultaneous users and process millions of transactions.
CSCE 415.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ITEC 352, or C or better in CSCE 146.
CSCE 415.subject: CSCE
CSCE 415.title: Mainframe Systems

CSCE 416.description: Concepts and components of computer networks and the Internet; network applications; network protocol stack.
CSCE 416.subject: CSCE
CSCE 416.title: Introduction to Computer Networks

CSCE 490.description: Major team-based software design project to be undertaken in a student’s final year of study; project planning, software requirements analysis, design, and specification. Written reports and oral presentations in a technical setting.
CSCE 490.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in CSCE 240.
CSCE 490.subject: CSCE
CSCE 490.title: Capstone Computing Project I

CSCE 491.description: Advanced computer systems engineering. Team projects. Written reports and oral presentations in a technical setting.
CSCE 491.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in CSCE 240, CSCE 313, CSCE 611.
CSCE 491.subject: CSCE
CSCE 491.title: Capstone Computer Engineering Project

CSCE 492.description: Continuation of CSCE 490 . Computer system implementation, testing, verification and validation of results. Written reports and oral presentations in a technical setting.
CSCE 492.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in CSCE 240, CSCE 350, and CSCE 490.
CSCE 492.subject: CSCE
CSCE 492.title: Capstone Computing Project II

CSCE 498.description: Individual investigation or study of special topics. At most three credits may be applied toward a degree. Approval of project proposal by instructor and department advisor.
CSCE 498.subject: CSCE
CSCE 498.title: Independent Study

CSCE 500.description: Concepts and properties of algorithms; programming exercises with emphasis on good programming habits. Credit may not be received for both CSCE 500 and CSCE 145 . Open to all majors. May not be used for major credit by computer science and engineering majors.
CSCE 500.subject: CSCE
CSCE 500.title: Computer Programming and Applications

CSCE 510.description: System software such as command language interpreters, client-server applications, debuggers; mail systems, browsers, macroprocessors, and revision control systems; file systems, processes, threads, and interprocess communication.
CSCE 510.subject: CSCE
CSCE 510.title: System Programming

CSCE 512.description: Measuring, modeling, analyzing, and predicting performance of computer systems and networks; bottleneck analysis; Markovian queuing systems and networks; use of operational and probabilistic models.
CSCE 512.subject: CSCE
CSCE 512.title: System Performance Evaluation

CSCE 513.description: Design methodology; processor design; computer arithmetic: algorithms for addition, multiplication, floating point arithmetic; microprogrammed control; memory organization; introduction to parallel architectures.
CSCE 513.subject: CSCE
CSCE 513.title: Computer Architecture

CSCE 515.description: Computer networks and communication protocols; socket programming; interprocess communication; development of network software; case studies.
CSCE 515.subject: CSCE
CSCE 515.title: Computer Network Programming

CSCE 516.description: Structure, design, and analysis of computer networks; ISO/OSI network architecture.
CSCE 516.subject: CSCE
CSCE 516.title: Computer Networks

CSCE 517.description: Methodical approaches for collecting and preserving evidence of computer crimes. Foundational concepts such as file system structures, MAC times, and network protocols; tools for extracting evidence; general legal issues.
CSCE 517.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 215.
CSCE 517.subject: CSCE
CSCE 517.title: Computer Crime and Forensics

CSCE 518.description: Fundamental principles and techniques of ethical hacking, including penetration testing life cycle, planning and scoping, identifying targets and goals, active and passive reconnaissance, enumeration and scanning, exploitation, post-exploitation, and results reporting.
CSCE 518.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: CSCE 215 or previous Linux/UNIX experience.
CSCE 518.subject: CSCE
CSCE 518.title: Ethical Hacking

CSCE 520.description: Database management systems; database design and implementation; security, integrity, and privacy.
CSCE 520.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 145, CSCE 104, or CSCE 106; C or better in MATH 142, MATH 170, MATH 172, or MATH 174.
CSCE 520.subject: CSCE
CSCE 520.title: Database System Design

CSCE 522.description: Threats to information resources and appropriate countermeasures. Cryptography, identification and authentication, access control models and mechanisms, multilevel database security, steganography, Internet security, and intrusion detection and prevention.
CSCE 522.subject: CSCE
CSCE 522.title: Information Security Principles

CSCE 526.description: Cooperative information systems and service-oriented computing. Techniques for achieving coordinated behavior among a decentralized group of information system components. Distributed databases, multiagent systems, conceptual modeling, Web services, and applications.
CSCE 526.subject: CSCE
CSCE 526.title: Service Oriented Computing

CSCE 531.description: Techniques for design and implementation of compilers, including lexical analysis, parsing, syntax-directed translation, and symbol table management.
CSCE 531.subject: CSCE
CSCE 531.title: Compiler Construction

CSCE 544.description: Functional programming as a paradigm. History of functional languages from Lisp to the present. Programming in Haskell, ML, or similar language at an intermediate level: recursive and higher-order functions, list comprehensions, types and classes, monads, lazy evaluation, reasoning about programs.
CSCE 544.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 330, CSCE 350, or MATH 374.
CSCE 544.subject: CSCE
CSCE 544.title: Functional Programming

CSCE 546.description: Development of mobile applications, including user interface design for mobile, local and cloud data storage techniques, and application architectures.
CSCE 546.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: CSCE 240 or previous programming experience with one of the following programming languages (C/C++, Java, Swift, Python, Matlab, Javascript).
CSCE 546.subject: CSCE
CSCE 546.title: Mobile Application Development

CSCE 547.description: Object-oriented methods and tools for application programming with graphically interactive operating systems.
CSCE 547.subject: CSCE
CSCE 547.title: Windows Programming

CSCE 548.description: Construction of software systems resistant to vulnerabilities and attacks. Cryptographic tools. Language, operating system, and network security. Case studies. Development of best practices through programming assignments.
CSCE 548.subject: CSCE
CSCE 548.title: Building Secure Software

CSCE 551.description: Basic theoretical principles of computing as modeled by formal languages and automata; computability and computational complexity.
CSCE 551.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 350 or MATH 300.
CSCE 551.subject: CSCE
CSCE 551.title: Theory of Computation

CSCE 552.description: Design and development of computer games, with emphasis on the technologies used. Hands-on development of computer games.
CSCE 552.subject: CSCE
CSCE 552.title: Computer Game Development

CSCE 555.description: Concepts, algorithms and tools for important problems in Bioinformatics, including nucleotide and amino acid sequence alignment, DNA fragment assembly, phylogenetic reconstruction, and protein structure visualization and assessment.
CSCE 555.subject: CSCE
CSCE 555.title: Algorithms in Bioinformatics

CSCE 556.description: Hand-on introduction in Python to the analysis of experimental data (biosignals, sensor readings, etc.), including various aspects such as data wrangling, time-series handling, statistics, classification, and visualization.
CSCE 556.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 240 or CSCE 106.
CSCE 556.subject: CSCE
CSCE 556.title: Analysis of Experimental Data in Python

CSCE 557.description: Design of secret codes for secure communication, including encryption and integrity verification: ciphers, cryptographic hashing, and public key cryptosystems such as RSA. Mathematical principles underlying encryption. Code-breaking techniques. Cryptographic protocols.
CSCE 557.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 145 or MATH 241, and at least one of CSCE 355, MATH 300 or MATH 374.
CSCE 557.subject: CSCE
CSCE 557.title: Introduction to Cryptography

CSCE 561.description: Interpolation and approximation of functions; solution of algebraic equations; numerical differentiation and integration; numerical solutions of ordinary differential equations and boundary value problems; computer implementation of algorithms.
CSCE 561.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 520 or in both MATH 242 and MATH 344.
CSCE 561.subject: CSCE
CSCE 561.title: Numerical Analysis

CSCE 563.description: Computer simulation of real systems; principles of system organization; random number generation; programming exercises in a simulation language.
CSCE 563.subject: CSCE
CSCE 563.title: Systems Simulation

CSCE 564.description: Parallel algorithms; scientific visualization; techniques for solving scientific problems.
CSCE 564.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: MATH 526, CSCE 146 or CSCE 207 or CSCE 500.
CSCE 564.subject: CSCE
CSCE 564.title: Computational Science

CSCE 565.description: Graphics hardware; graphics primitives; two-dimensional and three-dimensional viewing; basic modeling.
CSCE 565.subject: CSCE
CSCE 565.title: Introduction to Computer Graphics

CSCE 567.description: Scientific visualization tools as applied to sampled and generated data; methods for data manipulation and representation; investigation of visualization techniques.
CSCE 567.subject: CSCE
CSCE 567.title: Visualization Tools

CSCE 569.description: Architecture and interconnection of parallel computers; parallel programming models and applications; issues in high-performance computing; programming of parallel computers.
CSCE 569.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: knowledge of programming in a high-level language; C or better in MATH 344 or MATH 544.
CSCE 569.subject: CSCE
CSCE 569.title: Parallel Computing

CSCE 571.description: Foundational techniques in multidisciplinary software development, specifically of applications designed to present sensitive, sometimes controversial, materials in ways to engender empathic awareness of the interactor.
CSCE 571.subject: CSCE
CSCE 571.title: Critical Interactives

CSCE 572.description: Interdisciplinary approach to interaction design, user-centered design, human abilities, survey development, experimental study methodology, heuristic evaluations, usability testing, universal design, and accessibility.
CSCE 572.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Undergraduate or graduate standing in CSE or permission of the instructor.
CSCE 572.subject: CSCE
CSCE 572.title: Human-Computer Interaction

CSCE 574.description: Design and application of robotic systems; emphasis on mobile robots and intelligent machines.
CSCE 574.subject: CSCE
CSCE 574.title: Robotics

CSCE 578.description: Text and natural language processing; formal models and data structures appropriate for text processing; selected topics in computational linguistics, stylistics, and content analysis.
CSCE 578.subject: CSCE
CSCE 578.title: Text Processing

CSCE 580.description: Heuristic problem solving, theorem proving, and knowledge representation, including the use of appropriate programming languages and tools.
CSCE 580.subject: CSCE
CSCE 580.title: Artificial Intelligence

CSCE 581.description: AI Trust – responsible/ethical technology, fairness/ lack of bias, explanations (XAI), machine learning, reasoning, software testing, data quality and provenance, tools and projects.
CSCE 581.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 240 and CSCE 350.
CSCE 581.subject: CSCE
CSCE 581.title: Trusted Artificial Intelligence

CSCE 582.description: Normative approaches to uncertainty in artificial intelligence. Probabilistic and causal modeling with Bayesian networks and influence diagrams. Applications in decision analysis and support. Algorithms for probability update in graphical models.
CSCE 582.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in either CSCE 106 or CSCE 145 and either STAT 509 or STAT 515.
CSCE 582.subject: CSCE
CSCE 582.title: Bayesian Networks and Decision Graphs

CSCE 583.description: Introduction to fundamentals of machine learning with emphasis on how to use these technologies. Topics include supervised learning, decision trees, neural networks, deep learning.
CSCE 583.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 104, CSCE 106, or CSCE 145.
CSCE 583.subject: CSCE
CSCE 583.title: Applied Machine Learning Using Python

CSCE 584.description: Introduction to artificial neural networks, neural network topologies, neural network learning paradigms, training rules, and applications across supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning tasks.
CSCE 584.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 240 or CSCE 556; C or better in MATH 241; C or better in MATH 344.
CSCE 584.subject: CSCE
CSCE 584.title: Neural Networks and Their Applications

CSCE 585.description: Design and implementation of machine learning systems, Deep learning systems stack, machine learning platforms, scalable and distributed machine learning.
CSCE 585.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 240 or CSCE 106.
CSCE 585.subject: CSCE
CSCE 585.title: Machine Learning Systems

CSCE 587.description: Foundational techniques and tools required for data science and big data analytics. Concepts, principles, and techniques applicable to any technology and industry for establishing a baseline that can be enhanced by future study.
CSCE 587.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in STAT 301, STAT 509, STAT 513, or STAT 515.
CSCE 587.subject: CSCE
CSCE 587.title: Big Data Analytics

CSCE 588.description: Theory and application of machine learning. Current mainstream programming libraries such as in Python, and implementation of regression, clustering, principal components, and linear discriminant analysis. Detailed coverage of methods such as random forests, support vector machines, and k-nearest neighbors. Introduction to neural networks.
CSCE 588.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 106; C or better in STAT 530, CSCE 587, or STAT 587; C or better in MATH 241, MATH 328, MATH 344, or MATH 544.
CSCE 588.subject: CSCE
CSCE 588.title: Advanced Machine Learning with Implementation

CSCE 590.description: Reading and research on selected topics in information technology. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of courses by title. May be repeated for credit as topics vary.
CSCE 590.subject: CSCE
CSCE 590.title: Topics in Information Technology

CSCE 594.description: Strategic management and use of information systems in organizations.
CSCE 594.subject: CSCE
CSCE 594.title: Strategic Management of Information Systems

CSCE 611.description: Design techniques for logic systems; emphasis on higher-level CAD tools such as hardware description languages and functional modeling.
CSCE 611.subject: CSCE
CSCE 611.title: Advanced Digital Design

CSCE 612.description: VLSI design process models, introduction to EDA tools, HDL modeling and simulation, logic synthesis and simulation, benchmark design projects.
CSCE 612.subject: CSCE
CSCE 612.title: VLSI System Design

CSCE 613.description: Design of VLSI circuits, including standard processes, circuit design, layout, and CAD tools. Lecture and guided design projects.
CSCE 613.subject: CSCE
CSCE 613.title: Fundamentals of VLSI Chip Design

CSCE 711.description: Operating system organization and interactive processing systems, multiprogramming systems, process management, task scheduling, resource control, deadlocks.
CSCE 711.subject: CSCE
CSCE 711.title: Advanced Operating Systems

CSCE 713.description: Architecture of high-performance computers, including array processors, multiprocessor systems, data flow computers, and distributed processing systems.
CSCE 713.subject: CSCE
CSCE 713.title: Advanced Computer Architecture

CSCE 714.description: Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) Systems, Edge AI Hardware, advanced concepts in brain-inspired computing architectures, neuromorphic computing algorithms and hardware, spiking neural networks (SNN), in-memory computing, processing-in-memory architectures, edge computing and neuromorphic computing applications.
CSCE 714.subject: CSCE
CSCE 714.title: Edge and Neuromorphic Computing

CSCE 715.description: Analysis of security threats in TCP/IP networks. Design of safeguards. Coverage of security threats at each of the OSI layers. Application of cryptographic protocols for secure communication across a network.
CSCE 715.subject: CSCE
CSCE 715.title: Network Systems Security

CSCE 716.description: Design of more reliable systems through the application of reliability theory and models; reliability modeling; design techniques; testing; and requirement specifications.
CSCE 716.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: STAT 509 or STAT 511, or MATH 511.
CSCE 716.subject: CSCE
CSCE 716.title: Design for Reliability

CSCE 717.description: Evaluation of computer system performance and reliability using reliability block diagrams, fault trees, reliability graphics, queuing networks, Markov models, and Markov reward models.
CSCE 717.subject: CSCE
CSCE 717.title: Computer System Performance and Reliability Analysis

CSCE 718.description: Problems of real-time computer applications in process control or similar areas; task scheduling; real-time operating systems; advanced interrupt structures; memory management techniques.
CSCE 718.subject: CSCE
CSCE 718.title: Real-Time Computer Applications

CSCE 719.description: This course focuses on the security and privacy issues associated with wireless networks. Various attacks against wireless networks and their defense strategies will be analyzed. Students are able to embark in research of wireless network security.
CSCE 719.subject: CSCE
CSCE 719.title: Security and Privacy for Wireless Networks

CSCE 721.description: Components of a database management system; implementation issues; query optimization; file organization; file organizations’ transaction management; fault recovery; security; system performance.
CSCE 721.subject: CSCE
CSCE 721.title: Physical Database Design

CSCE 723.description: Database design methodologies and tools; data models; implementation languages; user interfaces.
CSCE 723.subject: CSCE
CSCE 723.title: Advanced Database Design

CSCE 725.description: Structure, design, evaluation, and use of information retrieval systems; algorithms and mathematical models for information retrieval; storage and retrieval of textual data in information systems.
CSCE 725.subject: CSCE
CSCE 725.title: Information Retrieval: Algorithms and Models

CSCE 727.description: Current trends and challenges in information warfare. High-level analysis of information warfare threats, like cyber terrorism, espionage, Internet fraud, intelligence activities, cyber ethics, and law enforcement.
CSCE 727.subject: CSCE
CSCE 727.title: Information Warfare

CSCE 730.description: Approaches for specifying programming language semantics, including operational, axiomatic, and denotational specification.
CSCE 730.subject: CSCE
CSCE 730.title: Programming Language Semantics

CSCE 740.description: Current practices and research in software development, requirements definition, design, program testing and reliability, maintenance, and management.
CSCE 740.subject: CSCE
CSCE 740.title: Software Engineering

CSCE 741.description: Personal, team, and organizational software processes; personal and organizational maturity; application of software process and management concepts during software development, primarily at the individual level.
CSCE 741.subject: CSCE
CSCE 741.title: Software Process

CSCE 742.description: Structural organizations for software systems as collections of interconnected components: formal models and languages; design tools and guidelines.
CSCE 742.subject: CSCE
CSCE 742.title: Software Architectures

CSCE 743.description: Elicitation, analysis, and validation of software requirements, specification of software systems including formal specification methods; CASE tools.
CSCE 743.subject: CSCE
CSCE 743.title: Software Requirements

CSCE 744.description: Fundamentals of object-oriented technology; object modeling of structure, function, and time-dependent behavior; system analysis and design.
CSCE 744.subject: CSCE
CSCE 744.title: Object-Oriented Analysis and Design

CSCE 745.description: Object-oriented programming paradigm, including encapsulation, inheritance, reusable classes, object classification, specialization, and message passing; case studies and applications.
CSCE 745.subject: CSCE
CSCE 745.title: Object-Oriented Programming Methods

CSCE 747.description: Structural and functional techniques for testing software; code inspection, peer review, test verification and validation; statistical testing methods; preventing and detecting errors; testing metrics; test plans; formal methods of testing.
CSCE 747.subject: CSCE
CSCE 747.title: Software Testing and Quality Assurance

CSCE 750.description: Algorithm design techniques; algorithms and data structures for sets and graphs; time and space complexity; sorting and searching; NP-complete problems.
CSCE 750.subject: CSCE
CSCE 750.title: Analysis of Algorithms

CSCE 755.description: Formal models of computation, including finite state automata, Turing machines, recursive functions, formal grammars, and abstract complexity theory.
CSCE 755.subject: CSCE
CSCE 755.title: Computability, Automata, and Formal Languages

CSCE 758.description: Application of probability theory and stochastic processes to analyze the dynamic behavior of engineering systems.
CSCE 758.subject: CSCE
CSCE 758.title: Probabilistic System Analysis

CSCE 760.description: Numerical solution of equations and systems of linear equations, polynomial approximation, difference calculus, solution of ordinary and partial differential equations, least squares and sets of orthogonal polynomials, Gaussian quadrature.
CSCE 760.subject: CSCE
CSCE 760.title: Numerical Analysis I

CSCE 763.description: Concepts and techniques for digital image processing; emphasis on low-level processes that analyze discrete images at the pixel level.
CSCE 763.subject: CSCE
CSCE 763.title: Digital Image Processing

CSCE 764.description: Fundamentals of quantum information theory and quantum communications. Topics include: Postulates of quantum mechanics, classical information and entropy, compression of classical information and classical typical sets, quantum entropy and quantum relative entropy, quantum states discrimination, Schumacher's theory of quantum compression and quantum typical subspace, communicating classical information using quantum channels, the Classical Capacity Theorem of a quantum channel.
CSCE 764.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 344 or MATH 544 or equivalent, or permission by the instructor; and C or better in MATH 511 or STAT 511 or equivalent, or permission by the instructor; knowledge of quantum mechanics is not required.
CSCE 764.subject: CSCE
CSCE 764.title: Quantum Information
